analysis_plan.loop_value: governed versus single_shot on held-out delta. If the loop does not beat one proposal, that is reported plainly.
analysis_plan.null_handling: Recorded as measured. A void run is reported as void and is not retried with different settings to obtain a score.
analysis_plan.primary: Per task per arm: mean held-out delta across seeds, with the development delta alongside so overfitting is visible.

arms.governed: iterate: propose from the incumbent, promote only on strict development improvement
arms.null_only: semantic no-op variants, no model call. Must score exactly 0.0; verifies the evaluation path end to end.
arms.single_shot: one proposal from the starting solution, no iteration, no selection. The baseline that asks whether the loop earns its cost.

capability_claim_boundary: A local Gemma 4 E2B model repairing four small Python functions under a governed loop. This is a claim about a model fixing bugs on a four-task suite. It is NOT evidence of self-improvement: the model does not modify its own scaffold, weights, or proposer, and nothing here is recursive.
claim_boundary: A local model repairing four small deterministic Python tasks under a governed loop, scored on held-out cases. Not evidence of model self-improvement and not evidence of a recursive effect.

instrument.primary_metric: held-out normalised delta against the starting solution

predictions.basis: Deterministic reward, semantically identical programs. Held since E69 and re-checked here because it is the canary that caught E70b's contamination.
predictions.statement: null_only scores exactly 0.0 on every task and seed.

predictions.basis: These are small, well-specified edge-case bugs and the model produced valid programs 10/10 in feasibility testing. A language model should reach fixes the generic mutator could not, which managed only one task.
predictions.statement: governed achieves a strictly positive mean held-out delta on at least two tasks.

predictions.basis: The tasks are simple enough that one proposal may suffice. Stated in advance so a one-shot success is not later reinterpreted as evidence for the loop.
predictions.statement: single_shot achieves a strictly positive mean held-out delta on at least one task.

predictions.basis: Iteration and selection should not actively hurt. If governed loses, the loop is costing more than it returns on this suite and should be reported as such.
predictions.statement: governed's pooled held-out delta is greater than or equal to single_shot's.

predictions.basis: Feasibility measured 5/10 unique at temperature 1.3 with a prompt nonce. At temperature 1.0 the same model gave 1/5, so this checks the mitigation holds across all four tasks rather than just the one it was tuned on.
predictions.statement: No governed run is void: every one produces at least 4 distinct candidates from 15 proposals.

predictions.basis: 10/10 on digit_sum_graded in feasibility testing. A lower rate on other tasks would mean the subset restriction, not the bug, is what the model is failing.
predictions.statement: At least 80% of model proposals pass the candidate validator.

proposer.model: gemma-4-e2b-it-4bit-mlx via local OptiQ MLX server
proposer.prompt_nonce: an attempt index is included per call. Temperature alone does not produce diversity on this model, and neither does prompt variation alone; both are required.

question: With a live model in the proposer slot, does the governed search produce held-out correctness improvements, and does iterating and selecting beat a single proposal?
trust_boundary: The model receives the public task prompt, the current program, and a count of development cases passed. It never receives hidden cases, the oracle, the reference solution, or the held-out split.
void_rule: A governed run with fewer than minimum_unique_candidates distinct candidate digests is VOID, not scored. A run that never searched has no result either way, which is the distinction E58 collapsed.
